paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: this whole chapter is about who you listen to and who you fear. A stiff neck refuses correction, a flatterer feeds you sugar, and a hot temper blurts out everything at once. Proverbs 29:23 says, "A man's pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor." I've been the guy who shouted a batch was perfect before I opened the oven, so trust me, humble tastes better than crow, and crow doesn't even bake well.

The chapter also shows that how people live reaches way past themselves. "When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan" (Proverbs 29:2). Leaders who listen to lies, or who ignore the poor, pull a whole crowd down with them. Then Proverbs 29:13 says the poor man and the oppressor have this in common: "The LORD gives light to the eyes of both." So the Lord sees everybody, and He cares how the poor are treated.

So what do you do with all that, friend? Proverbs 29:25 says, "The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high." Many seek the ruler's favor, but it's the LORD who gives justice (Proverbs 29:26). Stay teachable, stay humble, keep your eyes on the Lord instead of the crowd, and I'll keep the ovens warm for you.
